input: Burst pipe under the kitchen sink last night. Water damage to the cabinet underneath and some flooring. Plumber has given me a quote of £320 to fix the pipe and cabinet.
notes: Textbook small escape-of-water claim. Reserve < £500, policy active, no fraud flags. Should auto-approve payment.

input: Storm last night took out three roof tiles, one has landed in the garden. Getting quotes from local roofers — one has estimated around £1,800 for the repair.
notes: Clear storm damage, reserve well above £500 but below £25,000. Policy active, combined cover. Fast-track to adjuster is correct.

input: Came home to find we'd been burgled. Back door has been forced open, laptop, television, and some jewellery are missing. I've reported it to the police — crime reference number is CR/2024/12345.
notes: Theft with police report already filed. Reserve likely above £500 (laptop + TV + jewellery). Fast-track to adjuster. Document request for proof of ownership may also be appropriate.

input: Kitchen fire from a chip pan that was left unattended. The kitchen has significant smoke and fire damage — fire brigade attended and have given us their incident number. We can't use the kitchen at all.
notes: Fire damage with fire brigade attendance. Reserve will be high (significant smoke/fire damage, kitchen out of use). Likely total_loss or significant scope. Escalate to specialist adjuster. Emergency accommodation may also be needed.

input: There's a water leak coming through my kitchen ceiling but I'm not sure if it's from a pipe or from the flat above. My landlord says it's my problem but I'm a tenant, not the owner.
notes: Cover uncertainty — claimant is potentially a tenant, cover type and property ownership unclear. Cannot process without clarifying whether the policy covers this property and whether the claimant is the policyholder. Request more info.

input: Attempted break-in overnight — someone tried to force the back door but didn't get in. The door frame is cracked and the lock is broken. Repair quote from a locksmith is £180.
notes: Attempted theft with clear damage and a quote below £500. Excess is £250, reserve ~£180 which is below the excess — this should be denied, not auto-approved. Tests excess > reserve denial logic.

input: Heavy rain last week caused surface water to come under our front door and into the hallway. Flooring is damaged. The whole street was affected — our neighbours have also claimed.
notes: Surface water flood. Policy HI-2024-000002 has flood listed as an exclusion. Agent should detect the exclusion from policy_lookup and either deny or escalate for human confirmation. Tests policy exclusion handling.

input: I accidentally knocked my laptop off the desk and the screen is cracked. It was a 2-year-old MacBook Pro. The repair quote is £420 but Apple say it might be better to replace it for £1,100.
notes: Accidental damage. Two possible reserve figures (repair vs replace). Agent should use repair quote as reserve estimate (£420 > £250 excess but < £500 threshold). However, replacement option may push to adjuster for decision on betterment. Borderline case.
